notes: ACCESS ROUTE: curl_cffi impersonate=safari18_0_ios succeeded cleanly on the first ~10 requests this session (homepage __NEXT_DATA__, both search-results pages, and 2 category PLPs), then Akamai Bot Manager escalated to a hard block on this session's egress IP - every subsequent request (any of 6 TLS profiles: safari17_2_ios/safari18_0_ios/chrome124/chrome131/edge101/safari15_5) returned either HTTP 403 or a 200 JS-sensor challenge page (div#sec-bc-tile-container, Akamai Bot Manager markers). Tried translate.goog proxy (returned Akamai 'Access Denied' via errors.edgesuite.net - the Akamai rule fires even through Google's proxy IP), r.jina.ai (hit Cloudflare's own challenge on jina.ai, not usable), and WebFetch (403). Retried the block with 22-35s backoff across ~15 continuous minutes plus a separate ~3 min pure-cooldown window with zero requests in between - block never lifted, consistent with the H&M Home UK (S.N. 97) precedent of a session-persistent Akamai IP block. CATEGORY TREE: captured complete and reliable from the one successful homepage fetch, via props.pageProps.headerData.menuItems (Home department node, 17 top-level children) - this is a full SSR JSON tree, not dependent on further requests, so the taxonomy below is trustworthy even though most qty counts could not be verified. COUNT METHOD (for the 2 categories fetched before the block): props.pageProps.plpProps.productListingSectionProps.productListingData.totalHits, same field validated exact on H&M Home Italy (c134) and UK (c97) siblings. Plates: totalHits=37, pagination totalPages=2/pageSize=36, page 1 returned 36 hits with 36 distinct articleCode IDs - consistent (36+1=37), exact. Vases: totalHits=21, pagination totalPages=1/pageSize=36, page 1 returned 21 hits with 21 distinct articleCode IDs (e.g. 'Mini stoneware vase', category tag 'home_decorations_vases') - exhaustively verified exact. STRUCTURAL FINDING - NO LIGHTING, NO MIRRORS ON THIS LOCALE: unlike UK/IT/FR, the India nav (both headerData.menuItems and the deeper headerData.siteStructure flat tree, ~300KB of JSON, searched case-insensitively) contains zero 'Lighting' or 'Mirror' category nodes anywhere. Verified this is a genuine absence, not a nav omission, via the site's own search-results.html (srpProps.totalHits, same successful-request window before the block): query 'mirror' -> totalHits=1, and that single hit's title is 'Print-motif cotton T-shirt' (an apparel item with a mirror print, not a homeware mirror) - i.e. effectively 0 genuine mirror products; query 'lamp' -> totalHits=0. This is a false-absence-tested real absence (per project precedent), not a missed nav branch. The only lighting-adjacent nav node found is 'Furniture & Lighting' nested under Kids & Baby (kids-baby/furniture-lighting.html) - a mixed furniture+lighting roll-up that could not be title-scanned due to the block, so it was DROPPED per the mixed-roll-up rule rather than padded; this is very likely safe given the sitewide 'lamp' search returned 0 hits. INDEPENDENCE FROM UK/IT/FR SIBLINGS CONFIRMED: distinct locale (en_in) and distinct currency (INR, srpProps.currencyCode) captured directly from the working requests, plus this locale's catalogue is structurally much smaller/different (no Lighting, no Mirrors sections at all, vs IT's 7 Lighting leaf categories and dedicated Mirrors leaf) - a genuinely separate, materially different per-country catalogue on shared platform infrastructure, not a duplicate. TAXONOMY USED: 'Shop by Product' (the canonical flat product-type tree) was used as the source of leaf categories, not 'Shop by Room' (Living Room/Bedroom/Kitchen/etc.) - the room pages are filtered views over the same underlying product set with no unique nav-level breakdown of their own (no children in the menu JSON), so using both would double count; this mirrors the IT/UK precedent of using the product-type tree as canonical. EXCLUDED (by name/category, standard scope rules, no title-scan needed): New In, New In For Kids (cross-cutting/new-arrivals nav), UP TO 70% OFF / all Sale nav (never-extract Sale), Bedding (bed-linen: duvet covers/pillowcases/sheets/bed skirts/blankets - textiles), Interior textiles (cushions/curtains/rugs/tablecloths/napkins/towels/bath mats/shower curtains/blankets - all textile), Bath & Shower > Towels and Shower curtains (textile), Cooking & Dining > Napkins/Table Cloths & Runners/Tea Towels (textile), Cutlery/Kitchen Utensils/Chopping Boards (kitchen tools), Cookbooks (literature), Aprons (apparel), Decorations > Books (literature), Storage (all children - jars/laundry baskets/boxes/baskets/wall storage/kitchen storage), Room Fragrance (scented candles/diffusers - Home Fragrance), Premium Selection (curated marketing collection, matches IT's excluded 'Selezione Premium'), Sleep & Loungewear (apparel), Kids & Baby > Toys/Bedding Sets/Rugs/Storage/Towels/Blankets/Cushions (toys/textile/storage). 'Bathroom Essentials' (global-node-2.html) and 'NEW IN FOR KIDS' (global-node-1.html) are marketing-labeled landing-page slugs (generic 'global-node-N' URL pattern used sitewide for promo pages) that could not be opened to confirm contents before the block hit; treated as curated cross-cutting marketing pages and excluded, consistent with how 'Premium Selection'-type pages were treated on the IT sibling - flagged as an assumption in case a future session can verify. RULE 0: no lighting-by-room structure exists on this locale to apply the room-traversal rule to (confirmed absent, see above); 'Bathroom Accessories' and kids-room 'Room Decor'/'Tableware' were kept IN per Rule 0 (room/kids words are not blanket exclusions) despite the room-adjacent names, but their qty and exact scope purity (whether the bucket mixes in non-decor items) could not be verified due to the block - flagged for manual review rather than guessed either way.
